evidence.claim: Graham Holdings may hide education exposure through Kaplan inside a diversified holding company structure, making it a candidate for professional training, credentialing, test-prep, and higher-education services mapping, but segment materiality must be verified from filings.

Chegg remains a speculative shadow candidate for student-support tools because subscriber trends, AI substitution, churn, pricing power, and debt maturity could determine whether the model is recovering or structurally impaired.

John Wiley & Sons may function as a second-order education content and academic workflow supplier through learning materials, academic publishing, research content, and institutional subscription workflows, but current education revenue mix needs verification.

Udemy may be better mapped as an enterprise workforce-training and skills-platform candidate than as a pure consumer edtech marketplace if enterprise ARR, retention, and customer growth prove durable.

D2L may be an underfollowed institutional learning-management and workflow software supplier because it is Canadian-listed and sits behind schools and institutions rather than owning the learner relationship.

IDP Education may map to international student mobility, English-language testing, and university enrollment services, but the strength of the relationship depends on visa policy, placement volumes, IELTS economics, and country exposure.

Nerdy is a speculative micro-cap edge case for AI-enabled tutoring and live learning economics; liquidity, cash runway, CAC, retention, and institutional channel traction must be verified before it can remain in later layers.

The provided Serenity methodology emphasizes starting from the theme, decomposing demand and supply-chain nodes, identifying bottlenecks, mapping public companies, checking evidence quality, and defining falsification plans.

CHGG should be treated primarily as a speculative shadow/negative-control ticker for consumer study-help demand under AI disruption rather than as a clean bottleneck candidate.
WLY maps to academic publishing, research content, and education-content workflows; next layer should verify whether education/institutional content exposure is material and growing.
UDMY maps to enterprise workforce training if enterprise ARR, retention, and customer count offset consumer marketplace weakness; verify enterprise mix and net retention before upgrading.

D2L.TO is the cleanest institutional software/workflow candidate in this chunk by node fit, but evidence remains filing-dependent: ARR, retention, margin, customer concentration, and LMS competitive position are required.
IEL.AX maps to international student mobility, language testing, and university placement infrastructure, with policy and visa exposure as both catalyst and risk.
NRDY should stay only as a clearly labeled speculative micro-cap AI tutoring/live-learning unit-economics test case; liquidity and cash runway are gating evidence.

BNED has the strongest external evidence in this chunk for an education-procurement/workflow relationship through First Day and campus course materials, but micro-cap balance-sheet/refinancing risk may dominate theme exposure.

Need current public market data for GHC, CHGG, WLY, UDMY, D2L.TO, IEL.AX, NRDY, and BNED: market cap, liquidity, short interest, analyst coverage, institutional ownership, debt maturity, and valuation to complete pricing checks.

summary: Layer 2B maps the candidate chunk to education supply-chain nodes and ticker relationships. The strongest mapped relationships in this chunk are D2L.TO as an institutional learning-management/workflow infrastructure hypothesis, IEL.AX as an international student mobility and testing/placement infrastructure hypothesis, GHC as a hidden Kaplan professional training/test-prep exposure inside a diversified holdco, and UDMY as an employer-funded workforce-learning platform hypothesis. WLY is a second-order academic content and institutional workflow supplier. CHGG, NRDY, and BNED remain speculative shadow cases: useful for testing consumer edtech disruption, AI tutoring economics, and course-material procurement workflows, but their investability may be dominated by subscriber decline, cash runway, refinancing, or balance-sheet risk rather than clean education bottleneck exposure. This is relationship mapping only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
